title: Derivative of the integrated density derivative
statement: Let $I$ be a finite set, let $v>0$, and let $f\colon\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ be measurable with $|f(z)|\le1$ for every $z$. The function $m\mapsto\int_{\mathbb R^I}f(z)A_v(m,z)\,dz$, where $A_v$ is the mean derivative of the product Gaussian density of variance $v$, is Fréchet differentiable at every $c\in\mathbb R^I$, with derivative $h\mapsto\int_{\mathbb R^I}f(z)T_v(c,z)[h,\cdot]$; here $T_v$ is the Hessian of the product density, and the displayed derivative is the linear map obtained by integrating the bilinear form in its second argument.
replaced: Let $I$ be finite and $v\ge0$. Put $G_v(c,z)=\prod_i p_v(c_i,z_i)$, where $p_v$ is the Gaussian density of variance $v$ for $v>0$ and $p_0=0$, and put $S_v(c,z)[h]=\sum_i((z_i-c_i)/v)h_i$, with division by zero equal to zero. Define $A_v(c,z)[h]=G_v(c,z)S_v(c,z)[h]$ and $T_v(c,z)[h,k]=G_v(c,z)(S_v(c,z)[h]S_v(c,z)[k]-\sum_i h_i k_i/v)$. Let $f:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ be measurable with $|f|\le1$. If $v>0$, then $m\mapsto\int f(z)A_v(m,z)\,dz$ is differentiable at every $c$, with derivative $\int f(z)T_v(c,z)\,dz$.
